title: AI scams in Georgia and South Florida: How scammers use deepfakes to steal millions

reading.body:
Criminals used deepfake technology and generative AI to impersonate trusted people, including a real immigration attorney in South Florida, to defraud victims seeking legal services or money. This was not a failure of an AI system's design or training but rather the deliberate misuse of AI tools outside any legitimate deployment context. The scams succeeded because they reached victims through social media and phone calls where verification of identity was not enforced.

The failure to catch these scams lay in the channels where they operated. There was no system checking whether someone claiming to be an attorney actually was one, no verification that a voice in a call belonged to the person it claimed to be, and no requirement for victims to confirm requests through independent means before sending money. The scams exploited the gap between how people traditionally verify trust and the new ease of impersonation that AI enabled.

It is not established whether social media platforms, phone carriers, or other service providers had deployed their own AI systems to detect and block these frauds, or what such detection would have required.

summary:
Scammers are increasingly using artificial intelligence technology to commit fraud across the United States, with significant impact in Georgia and South Florida. Criminals are using deepfakes to clone voices, create fake photos, and impersonate trusted individuals including family members and professionals. In one case, a South Florida immigration attorney had his voice and identity stolen to target immigrants seeking legal help, while a Cobb County couple lost approximately $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam. According to the FBI's 2025 Internet Crime Report, Americans reported nearly $893 million in AI-enabled scam losses last year out of over $20 billion in total internet crime losses.

The financial impact of these scams is growing significantly, with Florida reporting 350 AI-related complaints and nearly $39.9 million in losses, and Georgia reporting 71 complaints with over $10.4 million in losses. Authorities warn that generative AI allows criminals to make traditional scams like romance schemes, investment fraud, and emergency phone calls far more convincing. Experts recommend families establish secret code words to verify loved ones' identities, verify urgent requests through known phone numbers, and never send money based solely on phone calls or voicemails.
